kinds.a: antivirus and security suite · internet security
kinds.d: Program that protects a computer or phone from malware and online threats; free antivirus, internet-security and total-security editions are one kind.

Program that allows or blocks a computer's or phone's network connections by application, port or address, sold on its own rather than inside a security suite. A firewall appliance is in Computers & Components.
Program or hosted filter that blocks or limits web content, apps and screen time for chosen users or devices.

notes: Antivirus software cut from 87 SKUs to 12 vendor flagships (the AV-Comparatives Feb-May 2026 ADVANCED+ products Avast One Free, AVG Free, Bitdefender, Kaspersky, Microsoft Defender, Norton, TotalAV, plus AV-TEST Top Product vendors ESET, F-Secure, Malwarebytes, McAfee; Trend Micro added as market vendor), with 10 further tested vendors as ranges. Dropped server/gateway, dead and mobile-only SKUs: AVG Linux Server Edition, Sophos AntiVirus for Unix, F-PROT, Vba32, ClamAV/ClamWin, Securion, Spyware Doctor, Titanium, Zero Super Security, Tencent Mobile Manager, Google Play Protect, Surfshark Antivirus, MacKeeper, Comodo, Dr.Web, IObit Malware Fighter, SpyHunter, Fortect, NANO, 360 Total Security. Firewall cut from 36 to 12: kept actively maintained consumer tools; dropped abandoned products (Kerio, Outpost, Online Armor, PC Tools, Privatefirewall, Lavasoft, Omniquad, Jetico, iolo, VisNetic, sunShield, Norton and Webroot personal firewalls, GoldTach, Karma, NeT) and small duplicates. Parental controls cut from 16 to 8: dropped Microsoft Forefront TMG and UserGate (gateway), GoGuardian (school), and spyware-style or dead tools (WebWatcher, Pumpic, DansGuardian, squidGuard, Green Dam Youth Escort). Built-in Google Family Link, Apple Screen Time and Microsoft Family Safety are not on any retrieved page so were not added; they appear only as the built-in OS type.
